recent_decisions.decision: v0.1263.0: THE ROSETTE MECHANISM CONFIRMED AND LARGELY CORRECTED - carve widths refitted against COVERAGE. (1) CONFIRMATION: pinning the mip to a constant collapsed coverage from a full cloud field to almost nothing - coverage is enormously mip-sensitive, and the mip a sample takes is set by its footprint, which on a down-look is monotone in the angle from the nadir. Coverage that changes with mip therefore paints a radial gradient centred on the view axis. That is the rosette, and the operator confirmed it appears in ALL THREE bisect channels including COVERAGE ALPHA, which rules lighting out entirely. (2) NEW FITTER coverage_width_fit: sweeps the carve width per level minimizing absolute COVERAGE error vs the level-0 truth (the shipped fitter minimizes the error in the MEAN of E[relu], a different objective - which is how it passed its own gate while coverage drifted +53%). Unconstrained it wants small NEGATIVE widths (total error 0.947 -> 0.408); the width is a DIVISOR in the hinge so it must stay positive, and the best legal table gives 0.947 -> 0.643. (3) MEASURED RESULT on the ladder: mips 1-6 drift went from +18/28/27/35/34/53% (a monotone CLIMB) to +18/18/18/14/14/7% (nearly FLAT). A constant offset cannot paint a radial gradient; only a climbing one can. flower-nadir - the vantage that has shown agate mip rings for the whole arc - now renders flat and unstructured. (4) FIXED A LYING HARNESS: coverage_across_the_mip_ladder held its own STALE COPY of the width table, so it reported the ladder of a table that was no longer shipping - which is why earlier width changes appeared to do nothing. (5) Shipped the F10 "Discard reasons" checkbox that was MISSED in v0.1262 (the plumbing landed, the edit script aborted before the UI insert - the operator had the flag with no way to reach it).

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1264.0: SUN TRANSMITTANCE NO LONGER DEPENDS ON THE CAMERA - the second rosette, and a genuine physics bug. cloud_sun_tau computed each tap mip as max(lodb, log2(seg)): the sun tap was FLOORED BY THE VIEW FOOTPRINT. Sunlight arriving at a point in a cloud does not care where the camera is, but lodb does - on a down-look the footprint is monotone in the angle from the nadir, so the sun transmittance at a FIXED world point changed with the viewer screen angle. That is a radial lighting gradient centred on the view axis, by construction. Replaced with a view-INDEPENDENT band limit: the tap own segment length, floored by the 260 m radiative-smoothing scale (the same constant the profile body uses - below it multiple scattering means the sun physically cannot carry structure). tau is now a pure function of world position and sun direction, and cost is still capped the way the lodb floor capped it.
recent_decisions.why: THE OPERATOR SEPARATED THE TWO ROSETTES with one capture set: at 2.7 km under a thick deck their COVERAGE ALPHA channel is uniformly white - saturated, no pattern at all - while DIRECT SUN and AMBIENT show an enormous radial flower. Coverage saturates and hides its own drift; the lighting does not. So there are TWO radial mechanisms: the coverage/mip drift (largely flattened in v0.1263 - ladder +53% -> +7%) and this view-dependent sun tau. Also confirmed from their discard-bisect capture: RED (planet-horizon cull) fills everything below the horizon when under the deck, which is correct behaviour for downward rays, not a bug. Rig: 3 regression vantages panics=0, FPS unchanged (60.7 / 82.4 / 53.1 ms), 53 cloud tests green.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1265.0: THE CARVE HINGE SPLIT - softness and signed threshold offset separated, and the mip drift is now essentially GONE. The hinge had ONE per-mip number doing two jobs: the half-width (a SOFTNESS, used as a DIVISOR, necessarily positive) which also doubled as the threshold shift, since coverage is P(body > thr - w). The coverage fit wants NEGATIVE shifts at mips 2-5 (those mip distributions sit slightly HIGH), a divisor cannot go negative, so the v0.1263 fit was clamped at its floor and left 36% of the achievable correction unreachable (0.643 legal vs 0.408 unconstrained). Added CLOUD_CARVE_T0..T8, a SIGNED per-mip threshold offset, applied as (body - (thr + T)) / sw; refit in the new parameterization; softness held uniform at 0.005 (the value the fit assumes) and T carries every shift. Degenerate 1-voxel level 8 held equal to level 7 rather than taking its arbitrary +0.1125. MEASURED ladder, mips 1-6: was +18/28/27/35/34/53% (a monotone CLIMB) before the arc, +18/18/18/14/14/7% after v0.1263, and NOW +1/+1/0/-4/+4/-8% - scattered noise about zero rather than a climb, and scattered error cannot form a coherent radial gradient. Total coverage error 0.947 -> 0.408, the full unconstrained target.

The constructed (voxel) bodies take their coverage from an SDF with NO mip dependence; the noise (shader) body coverage IS a thresholded mip. That is exactly the residual drift this fixes. recent_decisions.decision: v0.1267.0: THE CHORD NO LONGER SETS THE DETAIL SCALE - the inside-the-layer pinch. g_v2_foot_m (the per-ray footprint that freezes the constructed body displacement/erosion/warp mip) was taken at the SEGMENT MIDPOINT, m0 + seg_step*0.5, where seg_step is the chord through the slab. The existing comment above that line already ADMITS the consequence: "the surface DETAIL of every cloud on the ray changes by 1.34 mip levels along one screen row. That is a radial gradient - and INSIDE the deck it is the WHOLE term, because m0 collapses to ~0 in every direction while the chord runs from a few km straight down to hundreds of km near the horizon. Capped the chord contribution at CLOUD_FOOT_CHORD_CAP = 4 km (the scale of the cloud bodies): the useful part survives (a nearby surface is resolved finely) and the part that only encodes viewing ANGLE is dropped. OUTSIDE the deck this changes almost nothing, since m0 dominates by orders of magnitude - which is exactly why the artifact was always strongest inside. recent_decisions.decision: v0.1268.0: THE ROSETTE IS ANCHORED TO STRAIGHT DOWN, NOT TO THE CAMERA. The reframing that ends 5 wrong-target fixes. Aim the camera 40 deg OFF nadir and the pinch stays at the NADIR point, well below the crosshair; at 70 deg off nadir it leaves the frame entirely; at 0 deg it sits on the crosshair. Every operator screenshot in this arc was a down-look, where nadir and crosshair COINCIDE - so view-anchored and vertical-anchored were indistinguishable, and the governing heuristic written into PRIORITIES at v0.1267 (does a photon care where the CAMERA is) was aimed at the wrong variable. Structural cause found: cloud_weather_adv(dir, ...) takes only a DIRECTION, so the coverage field is 2D extruded vertically through the whole 1-12 km deck. Along a ray pointing straight down, dirp is CONSTANT for every sample, so the entire column returns one coverage value; oblique rays sweep many values and average. Field variation along a ray falls to exactly zero at the local vertical - a nadir-anchored singularity by construction. Explains every symptom: strongest inside the deck, faint from orbit at the sub-camera point, present in coverage alpha, immune to every view-dependence fix. NOT yet fixed; realistic-first candidate is altitude-dependent structure in the coverage field (wind shear veers the lookup with height), but note the finest weather octave is ~600 km against an 11 km deck, so physical shear alone may be too small - needs measurement before committing.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1269.0: shape-lod hypothesis TESTED AND NOT CONFIRMED (honest negative). Hypothesis: g_v2_disp_lod is assigned per sample from lodb = log2(camera-distance footprint), which violates the invariant written directly above its own declaration - Displacement is SHAPE, so every evaluation that reaches a given point in the world must agree on it - and since lines of equal distance-to-camera project to circles centred on the nadir, camera-anchored shape detail would paint exactly the observed artifact. The fine displacement octave rides CLOUD_V2_INT_LODC = -9.56 whose mip ramp spans about 1.7 km to 425 km, i.e. the near field, gaining a level per doubling of distance. Built the test behind dev pad bit 3 (F10 World-anchored cloud shape; showcase cloud_world_shape): pins the shape lod to a fixed world scale, CLOUD_V2_SHAPE_LOD_WORLD = -7.0, about 8 m of world detail. Result at 9.2 km with the clock pinned: spoke 23.90 camera-anchored vs 23.48 world-anchored, inside the 0.7 noise floor, and the step-comb frames are visually near-identical. The invariant IS violated and that is still worth fixing on principle, but it is NOT the carrier of this artifact. Toggle kept as a permanent instrument, default off. Also hardened the dev pad bit tests: chord_foot was w >= 3.5, a magnitude test that a fourth bit would have silently broken - same collision that already caught the shape-frame flag this arc.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1270.0: ONE CHECKBOX WAS DRIVING TWO UNRELATED JOBS, and that is why the static-versus-rosette tension existed. The F10 Spatial dither box set dither_on, which gated BOTH the depth jitter (where inside its step each sample is taken) and g_lod_jitter (the 2026-08-24 per-pixel mip dither, added to cure concentric mip rings; its own comment: the mip ladder crosses integer levels at fixed radii around the camera and prints those crossings as CONCENTRIC RINGS, and lodb is monotone in screen radius on a down look). The operator turned the box OFF in every screenshot of this arc to kill what they called TV static, which silently disabled the depth jitter too. Measured at 9.2 km, clock pinned, direct-sun channel: radial energy 23.97 with the box on, 28.11 with it off, twice reproduced (23.94 / 27.43) - the largest single effect found in the entire rosette arc. Now two switches. FACTORIAL (one sweep each, 0.7 noise floor): depth ON+mip ON 23.94, depth ON+mip OFF 23.74, depth OFF+mip ON 27.36, depth OFF+mip OFF 27.43 - the DEPTH jitter carries all of it, the mip dither carries none. Across altitudes the mip dither NEVER helped and once hurt (3.4 km clear 23.65 with vs 21.05 without; 9.2 km 23.94 vs 23.74; 60 km 14.71 vs 14.71), so its default is now OFF: a per-pixel random mip through the non-linear carve averages to a biased result whose bias varies with radius, so the ring cure carried its own radial signature. The DEPTH jitter default is UNCHANGED because its effect is SCENE-DEPENDENT: it helps strongly at 9.2 km clear and mildly hurts at 3.4 km cloudy (17.44 vs 16.02). Do not tune it from one vantage. Guards: jitter-factorial-34km + depth-jitter-load-bearing.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1270.0: the 6-agent shape-lod audit CLEARED every shape field as the artifact carrier, and its adversarial half earned its keep. Mapper rated the surface displacement octaves dominant; the magnitude refuter replicated the noise bake in JS (worley3, detail_bytes, box downsample, renormalize_level) and MEASURED adjacent mips to be highly correlated (rho 0.96 to 0.998), not decorrelated as the mapper assumed - so a mip crossing moves the surface 1 to 3 m, not 29 m, against clouds 85 to 760 m across. That independently confirms the empirical negative from the F10 world-anchored-shape A/B (23.90 vs 23.48, inside noise). Domain warp, erosion and the march step schedule were each refuted 2-0; the rind and carve hinge came back clean. Two durable facts worth keeping: the sun path never fetches the domain warp at all (g_sun_profile = 1.0 on every sun tap sets wn to the FBM mean), so the warp cannot be the direct-sun carrier; and the in-flight comment attributing the near-field ramp to CLOUD_V2_INT_LODC = -9.56 names the wrong constant - that is the interior TURBULENCE tap, while the fine displacement is CLOUD_V2_DISP2_LODC = -8.76. The invariant above g_v2_disp_lod IS violated in letter and is worth fixing on principle, but it is not this artifact.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1271 (in flight): THE ESTIMATOR THESIS, first measurements. Operator, after v0.1270.1: the rosette is present regardless of settings, most visible inside clouds; depth dither hides detail behind static; cloud EDGES always glitter and have never been stable since volumetric; maybe the way we generate them is wrong. Thesis: the density edge is a CLIFF (carve hinge width 0.005 noise units = metres of physical width; constructed-body rind 90 m) sampled with march steps of tens to hundreds of metres, so (a) each edge sample is a coin flip = the glitter, and (b) the estimator MEAN depends on step spacing, which is a function of the angle to the local vertical (dt_vert divides by r_rate, dt_seg scales with the chord) = a nadir-anchored pinwheel baked into the converged image that no look setting can remove. Built two experiments behind dev pad bits 5/6 (F10: Uniform march step, Wide cloud edge; showcase cloud_uniform_step / cloud_wide_edge): uniform step drops the verticality and chord terms from dt (distance-only); wide edge multiplies the hinge width x20 with the threshold shifted so the outer boundary stays put, and widens the body rind to 300 m. Real-render 2x2 at three states, one sweep each, clock pinned, depth jitter on, mip dither off: 9.2 km look-12: spoke 5.11 base / 5.21 uniform / 4.69 wide / 4.42 both, grain 5.01 / 5.24 / 4.44 / 4.54. 1.8 km look-12: spoke 3.98 / 3.96 / 2.60 / 2.66. 1.8 km look-3 (operator down-look): spoke 3.56 / 3.75 / 1.79 / 1.84. WIDE EDGE IS THE LEVER: radial energy -13% at altitude, -35% and -50% inside the deck; glitter -11% at altitude. UNIFORM STEP DOES NOTHING in any state (so the verticality step term is not the carrier; the cone term likely wins at these distances - workflow measuring). Mean luminance drops ~6 levels with the wide edge (coverage shift to correct). x20 was a guess; the right multiplier comes from the measured edge width in metres (target ~300 m, Marshak radiative smoothing). 6-agent assessment workflow wf_ef32979e-e14 running: measures edge width and step size, references Nubis/Frostbite, adversarially tests the thesis, designs the change.
recent_decisions.why: The operator asked the architecture question directly; the answer has to be measured, not argued, and it has to be the technique production renderers use.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1271 (in flight): WIDE-EDGE LEVER IS A NEGATIVE, and the first reading of it was a metric artifact. Round 1 (symmetric hinge widening x5..x150, threshold shifted to hold the outer boundary) read spoke -82% inside the deck and -73% / grain -55% at 9.2 km - but the strips showed the CLOUDS DISAPPEARING: with a 60x wider symmetric hinge full density needs body > thr + 2*sw, the interior never saturates, the coverage alpha kills the cloud, and the metrics fell because there were fewer edges. Mean luminance -10..-14 was the tell I under-read. Round 2 (asymmetric: inner side keeps sw0 and saturates where it did, outer side widens; constructed bodies keep the 90 m rind and gain a 0.35-density skirt): spoke UNCHANGED at both states (dn 3.59 -> 3.6..3.8; 9.2 km 5.24 -> 5.2), grain -12% inside / +8% at altitude. So a soft outer fringe neither removes the rosette nor the glitter. Uniform (distance-only) step: no effect anywhere; at these distances the cone term wins dt so the verticality term never engages. The strips also relocate the glitter: it is DARK PEPPER INSIDE bright cloud bodies, not stipple at silhouettes - i.e. the sun/shadow term, the same speck-sun channel that was convicted in the v0.1252 sandblast bisect. Both experiments stay as F10 toggles (default off) with runtime knobs in light6_color.xy (offset 304; NOTE the mod.rs comment calling the light5 pads unused is stale - 548 is underwater_ext, 552 is pix_ang). recent_decisions.decision: v0.1271.0: THE ESTIMATOR ASSESSMENT (7 agents, 1-D twins of the shipped march) settles the mechanism, and it is NOT the edge. (1) An ideal jittered march is UNBIASED in step length h for a cliff (E[tau] exact for every h 23..928 m; only exp(-tau) carries a second-order Jensen term). So widening the edge was never the lever, confirmed by three rig negatives: symmetric widening deleted clouds (the -82% was cloud loss), an asymmetric outward fringe changed nothing, centered widening changed nothing; and a FIXED 60 m step everywhere left the coverage-alpha radial structure intact (28.3 -> 29.8). (2) THE SHIPPED MARCH IS BIASED TO FIRST ORDER IN h because the march position t_cur and the sample position tm are two different variables and every endpoint rule mixes them: the SDF stride is measured at tm and spent from t_cur (overshoot up to a full step; first accepted sample 311 +- 280 m deep; 39-76% of 400 m clouds missed at 1.5-6 km), the coarse-entry backtrack rewinds to the step start not the last clear sample (h/6 of the sunlit front lost), the entry trapezoid runs against dens_last = 0 (h/2 lost), the first-step rewind lands behind the eye (h/2 extra: most visible inside clouds), and the exit half-step is dropped. Inside the deck h = seg/16 = 188 m / cos(theta), so every one of these is a nadir pinwheel in the MEAN, and the frozen per-pixel jitter makes each a static coin flip: the rosette, the always-glittering edges, and the dark pepper inside bright bodies (deep-first-sample pixels) are ONE cause. Twin with a sample-anchored march: bias -0.43 -> -0.02, sd 0.25 -> 0.087, identical across approach distances. (3) A distance-based step is a 1/cos(theta) law on a deck (distance-to-deck IS depth/cos), so no coarsening law can be angle-free; the ESTIMATOR must be made step-free first, then the step is a cost question. (4) Measured edge widths: noise path hinge 93 m at cumulus silhouettes with a 130-500 m (p50 ~300 m) visible ramp, already the radiative-smoothing width, leave it; the only cliff is max(CLOUD_BODY_TOP - thr, 1e-3) collapsing to a 1e-3 stencil when thr + T > 0.79 (floor it at 0.05). Constructed path: rind 90 m but the EYE ramp is 9 m (4.5-20) because CLOUD_V2_WARP_LODC = -5.2 encodes a 6.96 km tile while the warp tile is 0.19-1.4 km (honest -10.4/-9.2/-7.6), so the warp runs at mip 0 inside ~20 km and the silhouette is a 3-20 m inside/outside hash sampled at 23-45 m; the sun path skips the warp and sees a 62 m ramp on a smooth envelope, so eye and sun disagree, which is sparkle. Fix: derive the LODC per cloud like every sibling, log2(warp_tile/256). (5) g_march_max_km is never assigned, so for an in-deck down-look seg_step is the through-planet chord and dt_seg is inert. PLAN, in order: 1A sample-anchored march (bit 7), 2B band-limit the warp + refine rind/4 (bit 8), 1B+1C isotropic near step + bounded far angle term (bit 9), 2A normaliser floor (bit 10); delete bits 5/6; new map_diag 6 = first-accepted-sample depth, proven RED on base (a 0-600 m hash) before it may pass green; gates: diag-1 grain -50%, diag-2 luminance UP, cloud-fraction >= base-1%, the depth-jitter factorial collapses to within 0.7. Full text in the wxl89v22f workflow output.

recent_decisions.decision: THE ROSETTE, FINALLY NAMED (residual hunt wf_7b894dc6-a02, 3 mappers + 6 refuters, all returned; design pending). Suspect A, the sun ladder: CLEARED - coverage alpha never reads tau (a_i = 1 - exp(-sigma*dens_i*seg_len)), and the only stale global it leaves (g_v2_warp_m) moves the surface by a fraction of a metre. Suspect B, the temporal resolve and half-res upscale: CLEARED - at a parked converged camera the accumulation equals the march plus a uniform 3x3 quarter-res blur of at most 35% weight, which can only LOWER angular high-pass energy; the octa/map accumulation path is dead code since v0.1261. Suspect C, the 2D-extruded coverage field: the LITERAL averaging mechanism (wa constant along a nadir ray, averaged along oblique rays) is real but far too weak for a 28-unit fan and vanishes at pinned cover 1.0. WHAT IS THE CARRIER: every coverage-defining field on the noise path has a horizontal correlation length LARGER than the regime band height (weather octaves 95-1274 km, shape Worley 44.6 / 22.3 / 11.2 / 5.6 km, against band heights of 5-10 km), so each cloud mass is bounded by the band envelope top and bottom and by near-vertical WALLS on its sides that run the full band height. Vertical lines vanish at the nadir. Looking down from inside or just above the deck, those walls print as radial spokes anchored to straight down, and the clear corridors between masses print as radial slivers whose angular width is w / r_slant. That is CORRECT PERSPECTIVE OF AN UNPHYSICAL FIELD: a 2D horizontal spectrum extruded through a deep band makes vertical-walled prisms tens of km wide and 5-10 km tall, which no real observer could ever be inside of. All three physics refuters returned DEFECT, high confidence; an independent twin against the on-disk capture confirmed the magnitude. It explains every fact in the arc at once: anchored to the local vertical, present in coverage alpha, immune to sampling, lighting, detail-scale and edge changes, strongest inside the deck (walls tallest relative to slant distance), faint from orbit, and MORE legible once the estimator noise was removed. The operator said it on day one: the clouds at my feet are being sucked into a black hole at my feet. FIX DIRECTION (realistic-first): give the field 3D structure at the deck scale - horizontal correlation comparable to or below the band height, band heights matched to the regime (real cumulus is 0.5-2 km thick, not 5-10), and altitude-dependent placement/shear so walls are not vertical prisms. This is the operator multi-layer-atmosphere suggestion arriving from the measurement side. Design pending from the workflow.
recent_decisions.why: Eleven suspects were cleared by measurement before this one was reached; it is the only mechanism consistent with every measurement, and three independent physics reviewers called it a defect.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1276.0: THE CONTOUR PINWHEEL, REPRODUCED AND KILLED. Reproduced on the rig at 26.4 km look-12 weather rain (the first standing red vantage for the fan this arc has ever had: rain-26km-nadir, plus rain-26km-nadir-full). NOT a regression: v0.1271.1 (before the estimator fix) shows the same contour bands, noisier; the removed noise was hiding them. Not the iteration cap (0% of pixels at 224; 44-61 steps). Not the resolve (temporal off identical). Channel bisect: coverage alpha saturated white, SUN channel carries the bands, full res makes them sharper. COMB TEST: with the depth dither ON the bands dissolve into exactly the per-pixel static the operator disabled the dither to escape - so the bands and the static are ONE defect in two disguises: a deck-top entry whose depth below the surface is the march comb phase (the v0.1242 flower-ring class). Deepening the bisection 2 -> 5 taps changed nothing for exactly that reason (grain 18.2 -> 16.4). Fix: gate on the bisection stop width instead (seg_len > 4 * 30 m), and keep the 5-tap / 30 m stop. Measured at the red vantage, full res, dither off: grain 17.76 -> 6.60 (-63%), the contour bands GONE; what remains at the nadir is the soft radial elongation of the deck holes - the prism-wall content geometry the residual hunt named - with the inner-bin coherence now readable (+0.63/+0.47/+0.35) because the bands no longer swamp it. The operator swapped-areas impression is the same thing seen at two altitudes: at 58 km the deck is beyond the constructed-body range and renders as the noise sheet (speckle); at 26 km the bands dominated. Lesson: a guard added for cost that was not in the design silently disabled the fix at the one altitude range the operator flies most; the 3.4 / 9.2 km gate states never exercised it because their steps were smaller than 2*step_near.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1279.0: THE PROJECTION TEST SETTLES THE ROSETTE. At the operator bm-12 camera (1.63 km, straight down, just inside the top of the 1.0-1.6 km region) every remaining hypothesis was tested in one run each, clock pinned, and every one was a null: height-varying wall wander at 0.5 / 1.5 / 3 / 5 km (identical to two decimals - at Ultra the visible field near the eye is the constructed bodies, placed from the weather field and a cell hash, not the shape tap), sharp cloud base (0.5% of the band), interior relief fade (cavity / crown / pouch AO weighted by eye transmittance), coarse sun ladder for deep samples (skip rungs under 200 m), and every density component off one at a time. Discriminators: from 5 km above the same location the coverage channel is a SOLID overcast with no holes; the camera shifted 300 m or 3 km sideways gives a picture of the same style (petals differ, vortex identical), 30 km differs; extinction x3 takes coverage to 97% opaque and the interior goes DARKER (the inside of a cloud at noon should be fog-white: the in-cloud light model has no multiple scattering); the direct-sun channel alone reads +0.94 / +0.99 / +0.96. THEN THE OPERATOR ASKED whether a wrong transform (sphere projection, inverted frame) could be the vortex, and the answer is the synthetic checker (dev pad bit 21, F10 SYNTHETIC CHECKER density): density replaced by a known 0.5 km lat/lon checkerboard filling 1.0-1.6 km. From 3 km above it renders as a perspective-correct grid; tilted 35 degrees, correct; from bm-12 the SAME regular field renders as the rosette - one see-through cell directly below, everything else opaque, the lattice lines as thin radial slivers converging at the nadir. THE PROJECTION IS CORRECT, and the rosette is what any 600 m-thick layer of km-scale features looks like from just inside its top: the ray horizontal travel through the layer is 600 m x tan(theta), so beyond ~40 degrees every empty cell is hidden behind the full cells around it, and only channels aligned with the sight line remain - radial slivers by geometry. That is physics, not a bug, and it is why no renderer or content toggle ever removed the convergence: it cannot be removed. What is WRONG is the look of that geometry: (1) walls should be bright fog-white from multiple scattering, not dark shaded petals (the direct-sun ladder resolves nearby lobe shadows through the eye; extinction x3 darkens instead of whitening); (2) gap channels should not be km-long straight canyons between 5 km cells (real cumulus fields have 1-3 km cells with turbulent 100-500 m walls, so aligned channels close within a few hundred metres). The fix is therefore two fidelity increments, not a bug hunt: an in-cloud light model with diffuse multiple scattering (Nubis light volume / multi-octave scattering) and a field whose cell and wall scales match real cumulus. Everything built today stays as F10 instruments (bits 13-21, knobs cloud_hv_km, cloud_sigma_mul, cloud_shear), the operator bm-12 vantage is permanent, and the checker mode is the standing projection test.
recent_decisions.why: Eleven nulls at the operator own camera and a synthetic field that reproduces the artifact from a known-correct projection are the proof; the arc ends as a fidelity problem, which is what the operator said on day one - the clouds do not look like clouds.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1280 (in flight): THE IN-CLOUD LIGHT DESIGN LANDED (wf_49dd70c5-9d2: fidelity reference, code audit, three refuters, design). THE REFERENCE, quantified: cumulus LWC 0.3 g/m3 at r_e 10 um gives EXACTLY 45/km, so the regime extinction is physically right and the x3/x10 experiment is not a tuning direction. Single-scattering albedo >= 0.999999: a droplet is a near-perfect scatterer, so more extinction returns MORE light, and any model whose interior darkens with extinction (ours: 48 -> 31 -> 24) has no return path. Transport MFP 148 m: 150 m inside the medium the radiance field is near-isotropic and NO lobe 400-1500 m away can cast a visible shadow. Koschmieder visibility 87 m: 98.9% of an in-cloud pixel radiance comes from the nearest 100 m, so the rosette is a VEIL problem - the near fog is ~10x too dark (48/255 where physics says 170-210, EV 13-15 at noon, 15,000-30,000 cd/m2 in the top third) to bury structure that would otherwise be a 1% modulation. Interior colour is achromatic (sun colour); blue is a 150-300 m surface rind. recent_decisions.decision: v0.1280.0: BURIAL IS CORRECT, MAGNITUDE IS THE LIMITER, AND THE LIMITER IS THE MODEL DECK OPTICAL THICKNESS. map_diag 8 (burial profile, transmittance-weighted) at bm-12 reads masked mean 248/255: the in-cloud light engages fully everywhere the eye looks. Gain 2.5 on the source takes the masked mean 58 -> 101 (x3 extinction 108), linear, so the physical target of 135+ needs about 3x. That factor is the optical thickness: the source is Eddington two-stream on the LOCAL column, and the model column at envelope density s_carve ~0.5 is tau ~13 over a 600 m deck where real cumulus (LWC 0.3 g/m3, core density ~1) is tau 27; at tau 27 the design formula lands at 143/255 by itself. So the light model is right in form and its input is the model thin interior - the same thinness the x3 extinction test exposed (the eye seeing 600 m into a skirt) and the same reason the ocean shows through as slivers. DECISION: increment A ships as an F10 instrument, default OFF, with the gain slider; the FIRST item of increment B is a saturating interior density remap (density -> 1 within the core, coverage-preserving: the Nubis remap shape), measured at bm-12 by the same gates, after which A is re-measured at gain 1. recent_decisions.decision: v0.1282.0: THE ROSETTE FOUND AND KILLED (BUG-074). It was never geometry: since v0.1232.5 the per-ray cloud REGIME (family: band base/top, cover bias, extinction, tint) was read at the midpoint of the UNCLIPPED top-shell chord (kept unclipped by the horizon-seam fix so the family could not flip across the base-shell tangent). For any camera inside or above the slab looking down that chord runs THROUGH THE PLANET and its midpoint sits ~90 degrees around the globe in the pixel own screen azimuth, so the 8-19 degree type-noise cells printed as wedges radiating from the nadir, sectors whose band base lay above the camera rendered as see-through slivers of ocean, and the picture was right only toward the horizon where the lookup turns local. Low has no regime, hence the one clean tier. FIX: mid_dir = ro + rd * (m0 + min(m1 - m0, 4 slab thicknesses) * 0.5) - local for every down-look, continuous at the tangent (both neighbours far longer than the cap; worst jump ~0.1 deg, inside one type cell). MEASURED same build one line clock pinned: operator-bm12 inner-bin coherence +0.91/+0.81/+0.96 -> 0.00/0.00/0.00, slivers 2 -> 0, grain 1.03 -> 0.23, frame = plain fog (500 m inside a Cb-family deck, the honest local answer); rain-26km-nadir grain 1.99 -> 0.61; type-pinned closeup bit-identical (the control). WHY THE CHECKER MISLED: it replaces density AFTER the regime gate, so it excluded the projection and not this stage; 'projection correct => geometry => unavoidable' was a false generalisation, now recorded in memory. The fidelity reference also reframed the interior: the frame at bm-12 was 95% opaque cloud, the rosette overwhelmingly a SHADING pattern, and the extinction kernel 5-10x too long (chord integrals of 400-700 m, radial by construction). INCREMENT C (interior saturation, light5_color.w, F10 slider, default 0) ships as an instrument and is a NULL where it was aimed: on the stratocumulus deck (type 1.0 cover 0.9) it is bit-identical at the 3.0 km deck top (175.4/175.4, radial profile 146->207 unchanged) and 230.4 vs 230.7 inside, because at high cover the sheet union owns the field and C touches only cloud_v2_body - the same structural null as increment B (built vs noise path), from the other side. Deep inside a Cb (bm-12) it reads 39 -> 34, achromatic 0.94 -> 0.98: right sign, wrong vantage. THE INTERIOR TARGET IS ALREADY MET where the family is local: the stratocumulus ladder (3.0/2.8/2.6/2.4/2.2/2.0 km) read 175/230/218/208/191/153 with the in-cloud light on at sat 0 - fog-white 180 m under the top, darkening with depth - so increment A can be judged for its default flip at sc-inside-top (new standing vantage). The fix is a saturating density remap on the NOISE path (design B increment 1: Nubis remap so the carve saturates to 1 within tens of metres of the surface, coverage-preserving), measured by the sc-top radial profile (nadir within 15 of the surround) and sc-inside-top. RIG NOTE: two 4.6 km down-look captures in one sweep came out rotated ~40 deg about the nadir; masked statistics across captures are unsafe until the heading is pinned - use rotation-invariant measures (coherence, luminance bands scripts/cloud-lum-bands.js, radial profile scripts/cloud-radial-profile.js). recent_decisions.decision: THE FAR RUNG DESIGN (perf arc increment 4, the orbit speckles) went through a 5-agent panel (3 diagnoses + contract + adversarial critique, 1.27M tokens, 86 min) and the critique returned NEEDS_REVISION with 8 blockers, so the implementers were NOT launched on the v1 contract. Diagnosis of record: the speckles are the constructed bodies (cloud_v2_body) point-sampled at footprints 2 to 20x their size (CLOUD_V2_FADE_LO/HI 3.9/4.0 keeps them at full weight under 15 km footprints); the noise body is already band-limited by its mip chain, the built body has no prefiltered representation. The far rung = a planet-fixed PROFILE (per lattice cell and height bin: cloud fraction f and mean density G of the same field the march renders) in an RGBA8 atlas of six nested windows + one global equirect map with mips, read by lodb, integrated in transmittance by a clumped-medium element law (fraction + in-cloud density; a plain mean fed to Beer-Lambert is the white-veil class), skipping density AND the sun ladder at w=1. Blockers found by the critique and the orchestrator's v2 decisions (scratchpad farrung-amendments.md, folded into docs/design/cloud-far-rung.md by a revision agent): (B1) the bake cost was understated ~100x (uncached SDF point tests per texel: a level-5 bake ~2.8 s, the global ~85 s) -> A1 analytic per-cloud ellipses from a runtime CALIBRATION table (canonical archetype cross-section radius + mean density baked once from the shipped SDF), cell-stratified ellipse tests at fine levels; (B2) the element law was not step-invariant (ln T ~ seg^2) -> A7 tau_elem = sigma D L_elem, T = pow(1 - w f (1 - e^-tau_elem), seg/L_elem), with a prove-red on eco 0 vs 1; (B3) the shell draw's group 3 binding 0 is the temporal accumulation map, so the profile's group cannot carry the sun atlas there -> A8 a b14 override on the albedo-group builder, every group variant rebuilt; (B4) map_diag 1 writes OPAQUE greyscale, alpha is always 1, so three gates would have passed vacuously -> A9 luminance thresholds, calibrated red on v0.1288 first; (B5) the G5 speckle target (50) was below the metric's no-cloud floor (263) -> A10 at or below High's own count (252) and mass (0.152%) on the map_diag 1 render, and the census promoted to scripts/cloud-speckle-census.js (reproduces every baseline: eco0 2464, eco1 2989, High 252, off 263); (B6) albedo_sampler mip filter is Nearest -> A11 manual two-mip lerp on the global; (B7) the point estimator stratified over the cloud's box, so fine texels were coin flips and a_i was unbounded -> A1's inversion + clamp; (B8) no polar behaviour and no polar fixture -> A4 an ABSOLUTE equal-angle equirect lattice (no cos(lat0) scaling, no anchor) that degrades to the global's mips near the poles, plus a polar fixture and a truncation counter. Warnings adopted: A5 TOROIDAL clipmap windows (each level scrolls by whole cells, the exposed column baked the same frame; the re-anchor full-bake spike and its hysteresis are gone), A6 TIME-based refresh (2 s per level, 60 s global) gated on the MAX of gpu.cloud_profile over a moving fixture, A12 G1 floors per cloud_res arm (693/347/173 km), A13 the level walk + a non-radial instrument for the Chebyshev hand-off square, A14 the column C stored (3 column slices per level: atlas 6144x3584), A15 cloud_res pinned per fixture (the rig config drifted to 2), A16 G4-vs-High reported not gated, A17 an integration stub (constants + a synthetic-pattern bake + stub tap) committed to main BEFORE the implementers start so neither waits on the other, A18 seam scans by image coordinate.
recent_decisions.why: The design's worth is in what the implementers cannot see from their own side: shared layouts, the cost model, and gates that cannot pass on the bad build. The critique reproduced the census numbers itself and found three gates that would have been green on today's speckled picture; launching two implementers on that contract would have produced a merge that looked proven and was not. The amendments are decisions, not a menu, so the revision produces one coherent v2 rather than v1 plus a patch list.

ORCHESTRATOR READING: (2) is the sun-shadow cache WINDOW (48.6 km fine / 97 km coarse, planet-fixed so it reads as a rotated square): inside it samples read the baked ladder (real in-cloud sun columns, dark bases), outside they read the v0.1288 analytic column (CLOUD_LC_FAR_ANALYTIC = 1.0), which under-shadows a broken cumulus field (a mean-density slant column is far thinner than the in-cloud column: Jensen), so the far field is too bright and the window edge is the seam; the v0.1288 'look identical' check was made only at rain-26km-nadir, a stratiform case where mean and in-cloud agree. Shipped default, top fix. (1) is the deep relaxation starting at trans 0.5 (half the pixel's light still to come) compounding along long horizon slants; the economy's own rule is no look change and it was never measured on a horizon look at half res. (5) is coverage decaying with distance under the band-limited warp (a thresholded band-limited field loses its mean: the same Jensen class the far rung is designed around), so the DEFAULT loses distant clouds. (3) the anchored march is most likely the physically right one (the old march under-counted extinction to first order in h, v0.1271 assessment); the check is for any double counting. (4) the experiment couples alpha to the light source, which it must not; fix or delete. recent_decisions.decision: THE OPERATOR-REPORT WORKFLOW (wf_de0676a5, 16 agents, 2.5M tokens, 52 min; the F1 repair and the whole first far-rung run died on the usage limit, relaunched as wf_dda2f985) RETURNED: U1 (sidebar) implemented + reviewed + repaired (GuiState.cursor_free mirror, tab hidden while the cursor is grabbed, a close cross, focus-free slider readouts, two headless snapshots); F1 (the square) implemented: CLOUD_LC_FAR_ANALYTIC 1.0 -> 0.0. THE F1 MECHANISM OF RECORD (supersedes the orchestrator's 'analytic column under-shadows the far field'): the constant never governed what runs beyond the coarse window (the per-pixel ladder always does, cloud_sun_tau's !cached path; light_cache_tau returns w = 1 there); it only set the coarse outer band's blend TARGET, so with 1.0 the band ended on the analytic noise-envelope column against the ladder one pixel beyond: a hard step at wc = 1, reproduced on the rig as a BLACK BAND along the coarse edge (built lobes: the column charges the envelope crown the ladder leaves within a rung). The critic's cheaper third option (make the beyond-window path the analytic column too) was rejected by the captures: the band is far darker than the ladder on stratocumulus and congestus fields, so the analytic column is the wrong look for the far field; 0.0 restores the ring-free v0.1286 state at the v0.1288 cost (rain 26 km about 122 -> 152 ms). Both branches merged to main (merge-u1-f1.sh) pending the static verify and the rig gates. F2 (eco horizon darkening): diagnosis said the FOOTPRINT FLOOR (0.5 * t * pix_ang * eco: 29 m at 20 km to 231 m at 160 km at half res) binds in the horizon band and lands the first in-cloud sample past the rind; the critic voided its on-disk evidence (the 204600 sweep had the eco knob inert), refuted the ambient-ramp darkening chain (the ambient reads s_carve and h, not the 90 m rind), found the direct term's sign plausibly opposite (backlit at sunset), and corrected the coarse edge to 48.5 km; verdict: MEASURE FIRST (no valid horizon eco pair exists). F3 (distant clouds vanish under the warp band-limit): the diagnosis's 224-iteration-cap chain was REFUTED as the bit-8 mechanism (est || warp_bl saturates the OR, so bit 8 alone cannot move the refine; pix_ang was 2x wrong on the temporal path); the critic's mechanism of record: cloud_noise.rs:995 caps the mip variance-restoring gain at 2.0 while a 2x2x2 box drops sigma by about 2.83 per level, so the band-limited warp amplitude collapses geometrically with mip (mip about 6.4 at 21 to 63 km with bit 8 on vs 1.2 off); with the full-amplitude warp a grazing ray saturates in the partially dense halo around every surface and the deck reads farther, so 'more clouds' with bit 8 off is partly the halo artifact and 'vanishing' with it on is the collapsed warp; MEASURE (above-deck horizon, steps + coverage channels, both arms). F4 (in-cloud light transparent): no alpha coupling in the march; a bounded resolve-filter coupling only; keep the switch, relabel the row (light only), no shader change. recent_decisions.decision: THE D3 TOP-BOUND NULL DIAGNOSED (high confidence, third attempt after two usage cutoffs; read-only, measured on the v0.1293 gate captures). The easy explanations are REFUTED by reading the value end to end: cloud_v2_body writes the vertical gap into best and publishes it unconditionally to g_v2_sdf_m BEFORE its early return, the march reads it and converts metres by the same factor the body used (no unit mismatch), and the stride margin is about 265 m against gaps of kilometres (it does not eat the leap). THE REAL MECHANISM, in three parts. (1) The published plane is height * sy + br, where br is a HORIZONTAL cluster bounding radius (hundreds of metres to kilometres): a vertical bound subtracting a horizontal radius, so the leap targets a plane one cluster radius ABOVE a 150 to 400 m cloud and never the cloud. (2) The stride then overrides the base comb: the fix arm marches the whole 11.58 km nadir chord in 8.6 samples (1.35 km a step, ABOVE the 928 m vertical ceiling) against the 60 m reference arm s 192; and on exactly the pixels where the bit LOSES a cloud prod had rendered, the fix arm used FEWER samples than its own average (7.6 against 8.6 at 250 km, 13.0 against 15.1 at 60 km), which is the stride carrying the ray past the layer. (3) The value is published into g_v2_sdf_m, which is deliberately never reset when the body path is skipped (harmless for small near-surface distances, fatal for a kilometre-scale from-above gap), so it leaks into samples that evaluated no body. THE OTHER HALF OF THE BIT WORKS: the in-cloud footprint floor cap makes found clouds render MORE opaque, not thinner (the top alpha band at 60 km, prod 0.55 percent, fix 1.96, reference 3.75), refuting the thinning hypothesis; it should be split onto its own switch. AND THE GATE WAS VOID on its own written preconditions: the reference arm reads 8.55 and 8.35 percent coverage against its own 20-point bar, and at 60 km prod sits 1.24 points below ref against a 4-point requirement, so neither a pass nor a fail was admissible from it; the Sahara camera at cover 0.5 humilis does not put enough cloud in the crop to be a reference. FIX (4d, bounded): drop br from the vertical bound, publish into a distinct global reset every sample, clamp a from-above stride to the vertical ceiling so a miss degrades to today s comb, split the floor cap onto its own bit, and re-cut the fixture onto a cloudier camera with a prod-steps twin.
